source: The rules for reaching retirement money before 59 and a half, as the Internal Revenue Code and IRS guidance state them: the 10% additional tax on early distributions (IRC 72(t)(1)); its exception for a series of substantially equal periodic payments, the three approved methods and the interest-rate ceiling of the greater of 5% or 120% of the federal mid-term rate (IRS Notice 2022-6, superseding Rev. Rul. 2002-62), which must run the longer of five years or until 59 and a half; the exception for separation from service in or after the year the employee turns 55, from that employer's plan only, never an IRA (IRC 72(t)(2)(A)(v), the 'Rule of 55'); the five-year wait before a converted amount can be taken from a Roth IRA without the additional tax (IRC 408A(d)(3)(F), each conversion on its own clock); and the single life expectancy table used for the amortization and minimum-distribution methods (IRS Publication 590-B, Table I, as revised for 2022).
confidenceNote: Transcribed from memory of the Code, the Notice and the Publication, not copied from them. The life expectancy figures are recalled to a tenth and NOT checked line by line. Every path here is shown as arithmetic on the person's own numbers, never as advice; the Middle Class Trap room names the rule it applied beside each figure.
note: Read by engines/trap.js (K1, D-218). accessAge is where the additional tax ends. Rates are decimal fractions; ages are years.

sepp.maxRateNote: The ceiling is the greater of 5% and 120% of the federal mid-term rate for either of the two months before the first payment; 5% is the floor of that ceiling and the figure used here, so the payment shown is the largest the floor allows.

ruleOf55.note: Applies to a 401(k) or 403(b) of the employer you leave in or after the year you turn 55; money rolled to an IRA loses it.

singleLifeExpectancy.note: IRS Publication 590-B Table I (Single Life Expectancy), the 2022 revision, ages 40 to 65. Ages outside the range use the nearest end.

homeEquity.note: A home equity line commonly lends up to 80 to 85% of the home's value less the mortgage; half of the equity is the cautious convention used when the person picks 'borrow against it'. Home equity is shown and never counted unless the person picks sell or borrow.

verdicts.note: Trapped: a year the path cannot cover spending. Tight: covered, but with less than tightYearsOfBridgeLeft of spending left in the bridge at 59 and a half, or a penalty paid along the way. Free: covered with room to spare and no penalty.
